title: Canary autoscaler SLOs and burn-rate gating for GPU saturation backoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: As we enable autoscaler-driven capacity adjustments for Dedicated GPU pools, we need a coherent SLO and rollout gating strategy that accounts for transient GPU saturation and prevents canary traffic from triggering noisy rollbacks. This ticket defines latency/availability targets, error budgets, and canary burn-rate gates tied to autoscaler signals (GPU util, queue length, pod eviction events). Goals: (1) Define measurable SLOs for interactive and streaming routes under autoscaler influence, (2) Specify canary gating thresholds that use both telemetry and autoscaler signals, (3) Provide acceptance criteria and tests for CI and staging canaries, (4) Draft operator runbook steps for GPU saturation events and automated backoffs.
sla_targets: Interactive chat (hosted/dedicated): p50 <= 70ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 550ms (in non-degraded mode)
Embeddings batch throughput (dedicated reserved): 95th percentile latency <= 800ms for batch sizes <= 128
Availability target: 99.95% per rolling 30-day window for dedicated pools (excludes scheduled maintenance windows)
Error budget: 0.05% availability; burn budget policies defined per-customer grouped by priority lane
rollout_gates: Canary traffic ramping: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over a minimum 60-minute observation window
Autoscaler-signal guard: pause rollout if GPU util > 92% for >3 minutes OR queue length increase > 3x baseline
Burn-rate gate: if canary error budget consumption rate > 3x expected burn for two consecutive windows (10m windows), rollback to previous variant

Probe set: synthetic probes for 1) short prompt (interactive), 2) long prompt (streaming + KV caching), 3) batch embeddings job; require all probes within SLO for 3 consecutive probe cycles before next ramp step
Fallback policy: automated fallback to lower-memory model variant or reduced concurrency pool if autoscaler cannot provision capacity within 10 minutes
acceptance_criteria: Define telemetry metrics and dashboards for canary: per-route p50/p95/p99, error rate, queue length, GPU util, pod evictions
CI job (canary-sim) that runs synthetic probes against staging with configurable autoscaler stress; test passes if probe latency and error budget consumption are within thresholds for 30 minutes
Canary controller honors autoscaler-signal guard in staging and production; demonstrated in a staged run where GPU util is artificially raised and rollout pauses automatically
Operator runbook section added to console runbooks explaining steps for manual rollback, forced capacity scaling, and customer notifications
Documentation update: Console UI displays 'autoscaler pause reason' with link to probe dashboard and the offending telemetry
